subject: ophthalmology
title: Brushfield Spots, CMV Retinitis and Phakomatosis Eyes

steps.tx: **Brushfield spots** are pale speckles arranged around the iris mid periphery, a recognised iris finding in Down syndrome seen during routine eye examination. The spots themselves need no treatment and mainly serve as a phenotypic clue supporting the syndrome picture. Recognition therefore prevents unnecessary investigation of a benign iris appearance.
steps.say: Benign recognition together gives Brushfield understanding in paediatric eye clinics for children attending routine syndrome reviews. Pale speckles gives iris pattern additionally. Untreated observation gives correct management.

steps.tx: **CMV retinitis** is a necrotising retinal infection of profound immunosuppression, classically in advanced HIV disease with very low defender cell counts. Fundus shows haemorrhagic necrosis described by its pizza like appearance, advancing slowly with surprisingly mild symptoms until macula or detachment threatens. Low immune counts therefore make fundus screening urgent in this group.
steps.say: Immune context together gives CMV urgency in retinal clinics for adults with advanced immunosuppression and visual symptoms. Necrosis gives haemorrhagic pattern additionally. Screening gives macula protection.

vis.alt: Cytomegalovirus infection diagram with inclusion bearing cells.
vis.caption: CMV infection biology. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: CMV retinitis treatment combines systemic antiviral therapy with immune recovery through effective HIV treatment, plus intravitreal therapy for immediately sight threatening lesions near the macula. Retinal detachment from necrotic thinning is the major structural complication needing surgical vigilance. **Immune recovery** therefore remains the long term control strategy alongside antivirals.
steps.say: Combined therapy together gives CMV control in retinal clinics for immunosuppressed adults with necrotising fundus lesions. Antiviral gives direct action additionally. Recovery gives durable control.

steps.tx: **Sturge-Weber syndrome** links a facial port wine stain in the trigeminal first division area with glaucoma risk and choroidal haemangioma on the same side. Infants with the stain therefore need early and repeated pressure checks because glaucoma may be congenital or develop later. The stain therefore functions as an eye surveillance referral trigger.
steps.say: Facial stain together gives glaucoma surveillance in paediatric clinics for infants with port wine marks near the eye. Pressure gives repeated checking additionally. Haemangioma gives choroidal watch.

steps.tx: Neurofibromatosis type one shows iris Lisch nodules, lid plexiform swelling and optic pathway glioma risk, making eye review part of syndrome surveillance in childhood. Café coloured skin patches plus family history complete the bedside syndrome picture. **Syndrome surveillance** therefore schedules eye checks even when vision seems normal.
steps.say: Syndrome surveillance together gives neurofibromatosis eye care in paediatric clinics for children with skin patches and family history. Lisch gives iris clue additionally. Glioma gives pathway watch.

steps.tx: Retinal findings in immunosuppression must separate CMV necrosis from other opportunistic infections and HIV retinopathy cotton wool spots, because therapy differs completely. Immune status, lesion tempo and haemorrhage pattern guide that separation before treatment starts. **Pattern separation** therefore precedes antiviral commitment in uncertain fundus presentations.
steps.say: Pattern separation together gives fundus diagnosis in immunosuppressed adults attending retinal clinics with white retinal lesions. Tempo gives lesion behaviour additionally. Counts gives immune context.

steps.tx: Phakomatoses share a teaching pattern: skin or facial signs predict specific eye lesions, so surface examination selects which eye structures need imaging and surveillance. Sturge-Weber selects pressure and choroid, while neurofibromatosis selects iris, lid and optic pathway. **Surface selects structure** therefore organises phakomatosis eye clinics efficiently.
steps.say: Surface selection together gives phakomatosis organisation in syndrome clinics for children with skin and facial signs. Pressure gives Sturge-Weber route additionally. Pathway gives glioma route.

steps.tx: Anchors here: Brushfield spots are benign Down clues, CMV necrosis belongs to profound immunosuppression, and facial stains or skin patches select eye surveillance targets. Surface and immune context therefore direct the eye examination. **Context directs examination** closes systemic eye teaching for this group.
steps.say: Context direction together gives systemic anchors in examinations for students reliably in syndrome cases everywhere. CMV gives immune centre additionally. Stain gives surveillance completion.

cards.b: Benign pale iris speckles in Down syndrome; no treatment needed.
Necrotising haemorrhagic retinitis in profound immunosuppression; antivirals plus immune recovery.
Facial port wine stain means early repeated glaucoma checks and choroid watch.
